references.text: Egypt's sixth plague was boils (שְׁחִין) that broke out on people and animals, the same Hebrew word used in Leviticus 13:18 for an inflamed sore.
Boils from Egypt (שְׁחִין) are mentioned as a curse for disobedience, the same skin condition described in Leviticus 13:18.
Painful boils (שְׁחִין) on the knees and thighs are mentioned as punishment, the same type of sore referred to in Leviticus 13:18.
Job was struck with painful boils (שְׁחִין) from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head, the same type of skin condition that the priest was to examine in Leviticus 13:18.
Isaiah applied a fig cake to King Hezekiah's boil (שְׁחִין), and he was healed, parallel to the healing mentioned in Leviticus 13:18.
Isaiah's healing of Hezekiah's boil (שְׁחִין) shows the same type of sore described in Leviticus 13:18.
